description_en: Bhagavān Degaḥ is located to the west of Karuṇāmaya Mandira (BUN0001). It was originally built as a two-tiered temple and later converted into a hybrid structure with a domed roof. Bhagavān Degaḥ is partly depicted in a watercolour by Henry AmbroseOldfield, dated 1857. This painting serves as the sole documentation of the temple’s restorations and reconfigurations over the past 150 years. No records of its initial construction could be found. It can be assumed that the temple was severely damaged in the 1934 earthquake and was later rebuilt in its current shape. The lower roof was preserved but the upper roof was replaced by a plastered brick dome with a gilt copper finial. Later, the lower roof was rebuilt with a brass sheet cover and decorative eaves. The original open pillar arcade was closed off with lattice woodwork and a door was installed in the east façade. This work was probably carried out some time between 1980-1990. The inner cella was partly covered with industrial tiles and a new door and a steel scissor gate have also been installed for security purposes. Today, only a few of the original components survive; these include the carved pillars, corbels and cross beams. Most of the edge stones and original tile floors have been lost.Until a few decades ago this temple was known as the Sṛṣṭikāntā Lokeśvara Temple. Even the 2002 bookCultural Heritage of Bungmati(in p. 53) refers to it as the temple of Sṛṣṭikāntā Lokeśvara. A statue of Śākyamuni Buddha was enshrined in this temple around four decades ago. Before this, the sanctum of the temple was empty. The temple's new name of Bhagavān Degaḥ is closely related to this new deity.Elderly people in Bungmati tell of a legend which links this temple with the Sṛṣṭikāntā Lokeśvara Temple of Nālā (in the Kabhrepalnacok district). According to this story, the idol of Sṛṣṭikāntā Lokeśvara (which is currently in Nālā) was originally to be found in this temple. Some time ago, the idol disappeared from the temple of Bungmati. Eventually, it was found lying in the mud somewhere. ‘Nāla’ is a Newari word meaning mud. The deity found in the ‘nāla’was then established in its current location.Only the Pāneju Saṅgha of Bungmati have the right to perform the life-cycle(daśakarma) rites of Sṛṣṭikāntā Lokeśvara in Nālā. A group of eightpānejusfrom Bungmati goes to Nālā for this purpose every year on the full moon day of Phāguna. Like the temple of Nālā, this temple also faces east.Since the Buddha statue was established in the temple, two families of Śākyas and Tulādhara have taken on responsibility for performing the ritual worships. A procession now also takes place in Bungmati on the day of Buddha Jayantī (the full moon day of Vaiśākha). On this day, people place the deity on a cot and carry him around the surrounding area of Bungmati.
description_ne: उपत्यकाका नेवारहरू बुद्धलाई 'भगवान् द्यः' पनि भन्ने गर्छन् । यस मन्दिरमा पनि बुद्धमूर्ति भएबाट यसलाई भगवान् देगः भनिएको हो । गर्भगृहभित्र ४ दशक अघि मात्र बुद्धमूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको हो । बुद्धमूर्ति राखिनु पूर्व यो मन्दिर सृष्टिकान्ता लोकेश्वरको मन्दिर भनी कहलाउँथ्यो तर मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा कुनै मूर्ति भने थिएन । विसं २०५९ सालमा पु्रातत्त्व विभागबाट प्रकाशित ‘‘बुङ्गमतीको सांस्कृतिक सम्पदाहरू’’ नामक पुस्तकमा पनि यस मन्दिरलाई सृष्टिकान्ता लोकेश्वर मन्दिर नै भनिएको छ (Department of Archaeology, VS 2059, 53)।बुङ्गमतीमा यस मन्दिरसँग सम्बन्धित एउटा लोककथा प्रचलित छ । कथाअनुसार हाल काभ्रेको नालामा रहेको सृष्टिकान्ता लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति पहिला यस मन्दिरमा थियो । यस मन्दिरबाट हराएको लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति हिलोमा फ्याँकिएको अवस्थामा भेटियो । हिलोलाई नेवारीमा नाल भनिन्छ । नालमा भेटिएको करुणामय लोकेश्वरलाई अहिलेको नाला भन्ने ठाउँमा स्थापना गरियो।बुङ्गमतीका ३१ पानेजु संघलाई मात्र नालास्थित सृष्टिकान्ता लोकेश्वरको दशकर्म संस्कार गर्ने अधिकार छ । वर्षेनी फागुन पूर्णिमामा बुङ्गमतीका ८ जना पानेजु लोकेश्वरको दशकर्म संस्कार सम्पन्न गर्न नाला पुग्ने गर्छन् । नालामा सृष्टिकान्ता लोकेश्वर राखिएको मन्दिर जस्तै यो भगवान् देगः पनि पूर्वाभिमुख नै छ । यसरी हेर्दा बुङ्गमतीमा प्रचलित उक्त लोककथाले पहिला बुङ्गमतीमा रहेको लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति कुनै समय नाला लगिएको घटनालाई संकेत गर्न खोजेको हो कि भन्ने अनुमान हुन्छ ।यो मन्दिरको निर्माण एवं निर्माताबारे जानकारी पाउन सकिने कुनै अभिलेख मन्दिरमा पाइएको छैन ।ओल्डफिल्डले कोरेको चित्रमा यस मन्दिरको उत्तरपूर्वी भाग देख्न सकिन्छ । उक्त समय यो मन्दिर दुई तल्ले पेगोडा शैलीमा निर्माण गरिएको देख्न सकिन्छ । उक्त पेगोडा शैलीको मन्दिर सन् १९३४ को महाभूकम्पमा भत्किएको हुन सक्ने संभावना छ।मन्दिरमा बुद्धमूर्ति स्थापना भएदेखि शाक्य र तुलाधर थरका दुई परिवारले नित्य पूजा एवं रेखदेखको कार्य गर्दैआएका छन् । बुद्धमूर्ति स्थापना गरिएकै सालदेखि बुद्धजयन्तीको दिन मूर्तिलाई खटमा राखी जात्रा गर्ने परम्परा पनि चलिआएको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: The Buddha Dharma Saṅgha Nāmasaṅgīti Sevā Khalaḥ was formed. This committee arranges for Nāmasaṅgīti recitations to take place in the temple.
A painting made by Henry AmbroseOldfieldin 1857 shows this temple in a traditional two-tiered style. It can be assumed that this temple was severely damaged in the 1934 earthquake.
The Buddha Dharma Saṅgha Nāmasaṅgīti Sevā Khalaḥ offered alhegā(an outer garment made of metal) to Buddha.
The statue of Śākyamuni Buddha was enshrined in the temple.
